source.title: Towards a Unified and Verified Understanding of Group-Operation Networks
source.authors: Wilson Wu; Louis Jaburi; Jacob Drori; Jason Gross

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports that grokking time differs with optimizer choice, bearing on the optimizer-artifact version, but does not reproduce the original grokking measurements or control optimizer instabilities.
record.gate_note: The paper reports final accuracy bounds and causal-intervention outcomes, but those do not measure the grokking trajectory or the optimizer/numerical artifact described in the claim versions. It also cites grokking results from prior work; those cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The grokking content is incidental: the paper never measures grokking trajectories. It does bear on V6. Across 100 S5 seeds with identical hyperparameters, it shows that two previously 'different' algorithms (irreps, cosets) are facets of one ρ-set circuit. Yet only about 55% of runs fit that circuit exactly, and the rest deviate (a-bad, ρ-bad). This restates V6 rather than reproducing the original method. The Adam vs AdamW footnote is an uncontrolled aside and does not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Incorrect focus. The authors conclude that one-hidden-layer group-composition networks implement bi-equivariant ρ-set circuits, which unify the prior irrep and coset explanations. Compact proofs verify this for a large fraction (about 55%) of S5 models, and the remaining models mostly deviate from the explanation. The Adam vs AdamW remark is a footnote, not a conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: This is a mechanistic study of group composition on finite groups, with a reported optimizer comparison; it does not reproduce the original grokking study's method or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported time to grokking differs between Adam and AdamW.

fits_no_version.finding: Causal interventions give the same directional results on Z/53Z models, where the coset algorithm cannot hold, as on S5 (Table 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Causal interventions used to validate grokking-circuit explanations are weak positive evidence and cannot distinguish between algorithms.

record.problems: The optimizer comparison is not described as a controlled, matched experiment; exact epoch counts and uncertainty are not reported. The paper does not isolate optimizer instability or numerical effects.

untested.parts: No train or test accuracy trajectories and no training-set-size sweep. Appendix K.1 only remarks that small groups do not grok.
Circuits are analysed only in final models; formation over training and progress measures are not tracked.
No non-algorithmic data and no initialization-scale or weight-norm sweep.
Weight decay is fixed; no critical dataset size and no ungrokking. Fig 4 only correlates deviant circuits with higher weight norm.
Architecture and hyperparameter variation is not tested. Only random seeds vary, plus small hyperparameter changes for S4 and A5.
Optimizer instabilities and softmax floating-point limits are not isolated or controlled.

missing.what: Fraction of S5 runs fitting the ρ-set circuit (55%) vs deviating (45%, a-bad/ρ-bad); mean accuracy bound 50.4% overall and 91.7% for explained runs
Fraction of runs unexplained by the ρ-set circuit for S4 (48%) and A5 (78%)
All examined models satisfy both irrep sparsity and coset concentration
Models with non-constant projection vector a have higher loss and weight norm

record.verdict_notes: The record overweights a single footnote. Grokking is otherwise only cited (Power et al.). Appendix K.1 states that small groups do not grok because the training set is too small; this is unquantified and not a V1 test. Neither original source is this paper.

versions.untested_parts: No training-accuracy or test-accuracy trajectory, post-overfitting jump, or training-set-size comparison is reported.
The paper analyzes final-model circuits, but does not track their formation over training, memorizing-component removal, or progress measures anticipating a test-accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic data or initialization-scale or weight-norm sweep is tested for grokking-like delays.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is studied.
Weight decay is used, but the paper does not test an efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
The paper does not compare whether runs converge to the same algorithm across architectures or hyperparameters.

Optimizer choice is reported to affect grokking time, but optimizer instabilities and floating-point or softmax effects are not isolated, and the study does not show that controlling them removes the delay.

rows.subject: one-hidden-layer models trained on S5
rows.operation_detail: Compare reported grokking time for models trained with Adam against prior-work models trained with AdamW.
rows.baseline: AdamW; the comparison setup is not stated
rows.value: Models trained with Adam grok the task in an order of magnitude fewer epochs.
rows.note: The optimizer comparison is reported as an aggregate qualitative result; the text does not give separate counts or exact epoch values for the two optimizers. The authors also note that they did not notice significant differences in end results post-grokking, but give no numerical comparison.
rows.check: This is a footnote aside, not an experiment, and gives no epoch values. The two optimizers also used different weight decay (Adam 2e-4 vs AdamW 1), so the optimizer is confounded. Both are adaptive optimizers, and grokking still occurs under Adam. The row therefore cannot show whether the delay is an optimizer or numerical artifact that disappears under control. The reader's 'partial' state and 'supports' label are unwarranted.

relationships.condition: 100 one-hidden-layer models on S5, same hyperparameters, different seeds
relationships.reason: Text-based (no row). All models satisfy irrep sparsity and coset concentration, and the prior divergent explanations unify as one ρ-set algorithm. 55% of models fit the circuit closely enough for a 91.7% mean accuracy bound (Sec 5.2, 6.3, 7; Fig 3).
relationships.display_finding: All 100 models exhibited irrep sparsity and coset concentration, while 55% fit the proposed ρ-set circuit closely enough for a 91.7% mean accuracy lower bound.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: 100 one-hidden-layer models on S5, same hyperparameters, different seeds
source_check.reason: Shared irrep sparsity and coset concentration establish common neuron properties, not the same identified algorithm across all 100 runs. The detailed circuit explanation fits 55%, with a 91.7% mean accuracy lower bound; other runs have observed structural deviations (Section 5.2, Figure 3, Sections 6.3–7). Support for the detailed circuit should be restricted to the explained subset.

relationships.condition: Subset of runs deviating from the ρ-set circuit: 45% of S5, 48% of S4, 78% of A5 runs
relationships.reason: Text-based (no row). These runs show a-bad (non-constant projection vector, a suboptimal minimum with higher loss and norm, Fig 4) or ρ-bad (missing pairs, possibly numerical integration). The authors cannot explain these runs (Fig 3, 10, 11).
relationships.display_finding: Deviations affected 45% of S5, 48% of S4 and 78% of A5 runs, involving nonconstant projection vectors with higher loss and norm or incomplete representation pairs that the authors could not explain.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Subset of runs deviating from the ρ-set circuit: 45% of S5, 48% of S4, 78% of A5 runs
source_check.reason: The percentages and inspected circuit deviations are explicit (Figures 9–11; Section 5.2). Nonconstant projection vectors or missing summation pairs qualify uniform identification with this circuit. These findings do not fully characterize alternative algorithms.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study directly compares learned computational structure across repeated training runs, bearing on V6 despite not measuring delayed-generalization trajectories.

tranche.reason: The results qualify uniform circuit identification across runs: shared neuron properties coexist with observed departures from the detailed circuit explanation (Sections 5.2 and 7).

source_check.notes: The 91.7% figure is a mean accuracy lower bound for the explained 55% of S5 models. Separately, 45% of all S5 models receive a bound of at least 95%; incomplete explanations alone do not establish distinct alternative algorithms.

reader_labels.reason: The reported order-of-magnitude difference in epochs to grokking shows optimizer choice can affect the delay (r1), though the proposed artifact mechanism and its removal under controls are not established.
